chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, both together, from Ibn Mahboub from Nu'aym ibn Ibrahim from Abu Sayyar from Abu Abdillah (Allah) (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who killed the foetus of a slave-girl belonging to others, which was in her womb, he (peace be upon him) said: If it died in her womb after he had struck her, then upon him is half of a tenth of the value of its mother; and if he struck her and she miscarried it alive and then it died, then upon him is a tenth of the value of its mother.
ai.seo_question: What is the blood money for killing a foetus in a slave's womb according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of proportional compensation (diyah) for a foetus based on the stage of development, distinguishing between intrauterine death and live birth followed by death. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling is often cited to demonstrate the gradation of life's sanctity and the legal status of the unborn, linking the compensation to the mother's value as a slave, reflecting the socio-legal context of the time. It underscores the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his progeny) detailed application of justice in personal status laws.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, both together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Nuaym Bin Ibrahim, from Abu Sayyar,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who killed a foetus of a slave girl in her belly, (which was) for a people (not belong to him). So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it died inside her belly after her having been struck, so upon him is half of the price of his slave girl, and if she had been struck, so it was miscarried alive, so it died (afterwards), so upon him is a tenth of the price of his slave girl’.
